questions.question: What does Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) primarily evaluate in generative image models?
questions.choice_A: The distance between real and generated feature distributions assuming a Gaussian in Inception feature space
questions.choice_B: The classification accuracy of generated images on ImageNet
questions.choice_C: The mutual information between prompts and images
questions.choice_D: The pixel-wise reconstruction error between generated and real images

questions.question: Which is a key caveat of the Inception Score (IS) when used to evaluate generative models?
questions.choice_A: IS is invariant to the number of samples, so it cannot detect overfitting
questions.choice_B: IS depends on a pretrained ImageNet classifier and can be misleading for domains outside its label space
questions.choice_C: IS requires the ground-truth dataset distributions to be known
questions.choice_D: IS cannot be computed for conditional models

questions.question: What does the CLIP score typically measure in text-to-image evaluation?
questions.choice_A: Cosine similarity between text and image embeddings in a joint multimodal space
questions.choice_B: The probability of the image belonging to the most relevant ImageNet class
questions.choice_C: The Earth Mover’s Distance between text token distributions and image pixel distributions
questions.choice_D: The F1 score between detected and ground-truth objects in the image

questions.question: Which limitation most accurately describes using CLIP score for prompt fidelity?
questions.choice_A: CLIP score requires per-pixel annotations to be meaningful
questions.choice_B: CLIP score is equivalent to FID, so it cannot evaluate alignment separately from realism
questions.choice_C: CLIP score cannot be computed for single images because it is a dataset-level metric
questions.choice_D: CLIP score can be inflated by generic captions, style biases, or prompt engineering that does not ensure fine-grained content accuracy

questions.question: What is LPIPS primarily used to measure in generative image evaluation?
questions.choice_A: The overlap between semantic segmentations of two images
questions.choice_B: Perceptual distance between two images using deep network features, where lower is more similar
questions.choice_C: The classification confidence of the generated image
questions.choice_D: The number of unique modes captured by the generator

questions.question: Why are DINO features often preferred for semantic similarity or diversity analysis under domain shift?
questions.choice_A: They are self-supervised and tend to capture semantically meaningful features without being tied to a fixed label set
questions.choice_B: They exactly match the distributional assumptions used by FID
questions.choice_C: They produce lower-dimensional embeddings than CLIP, reducing computation time in all cases
questions.choice_D: They guarantee higher classification accuracy on ImageNet compared to supervised features

questions.question: Which approach best assesses diversity within a set of generated images?
questions.choice_A: Computing a single CLIP score per image and averaging
questions.choice_B: Reporting only the minimum LPIPS between any pair of images
questions.choice_C: Using statistics such as average pairwise LPIPS, coverage/precision-recall in feature space, or k-NN redundancy rates
questions.choice_D: Counting the number of unique prompt tokens used during generation

questions.question: In structure-conditioned generation with binary masks, what does an Intersection-over-Union (IoU) of 0.5 mean?
questions.choice_A: Half the predicted pixels match in color with ground truth
questions.choice_B: The area of overlap between predicted and target masks is half the area of their union
questions.choice_C: The model’s confidence is 50% for the predicted class
questions.choice_D: The predicted mask is exactly half the size of the ground-truth mask

questions.question: When evaluating edge or contour adherence, which practice yields a robust F1 measure?
questions.choice_A: Compute F1 at a single fixed threshold chosen on the test set to maximize performance
questions.choice_B: Average precision and recall separately across images but not F1
questions.choice_C: Use pixel-wise $L_2$ distance and convert it to F1 by a linear scaling
questions.choice_D: Report ODS (optimal dataset scale) and/or OIS (optimal image scale) by sweeping thresholds on a validation set

questions.question: For pose control via landmarks, why is it common to normalize $L_2$ keypoint error by inter-ocular distance or object scale?
questions.choice_A: To make the error comparable across images with different scales and camera distances
questions.choice_B: To ensure the error is always less than 1
questions.choice_C: Because unnormalized $L_2$ cannot be computed reliably
questions.choice_D: To convert the metric into a classification accuracy

questions.question: Why are pairwise human preference tests often favored over absolute Likert ratings in generative image evaluation?
questions.choice_A: They take less time per judgment in every setting
questions.choice_B: They eliminate annotator bias completely
questions.choice_C: They reduce scale-use variability and can be aggregated with models like Bradley–Terry or Thurstone
questions.choice_D: They allow direct computation of FID from human labels

questions.question: What is the main reason to average metrics over multiple random seeds when evaluating generative models?
questions.choice_A: To increase the metric values by smoothing
questions.choice_B: To reduce variance due to stochastic training or sampling and obtain a more reliable estimate
questions.choice_C: To avoid the need for statistical testing
questions.choice_D: To ensure reproducibility without sharing code

questions.question: You compare two models’ FID across the same set of random seeds. Which analysis is most appropriate?
questions.choice_A: Use an unpaired t-test because the metrics are independent
questions.choice_B: Report only the best seed for each model to avoid averaging bias
questions.choice_C: Use a permutation test that shuffles images between models
questions.choice_D: Use a paired test or paired bootstrap to account for matched seeds and report confidence intervals

questions.question: When evaluating across many prompts and reporting multiple p-values, which practice best controls false discoveries?
questions.choice_A: Apply a multiple comparisons correction such as Benjamini–Hochberg to control the false discovery rate
questions.choice_B: Ignore non-significant p-values and report only significant ones
questions.choice_C: Increase the sample size until all results are significant
questions.choice_D: Average p-values across tests to obtain a single summary statistic

questions.question: Which statement about sample size effects on FID is most accurate?
questions.choice_A: FID is unbiased even for very small sample sizes
questions.choice_B: FID increases monotonically with more samples for any model
questions.choice_C: FID is biased for small sample sizes and stabilizes as the number of samples (often tens of thousands) increases
questions.choice_D: FID does not depend on the number of samples if IS is also reported

questions.question: What is a sound protocol when using CLIP for text-image alignment evaluation in models also trained with CLIP-based losses?
questions.choice_A: Always use the exact same CLIP checkpoint used during training to maximize alignment
questions.choice_B: Use a held-out CLIP variant or complementary alignment checks to mitigate evaluator–model coupling and overfitting
questions.choice_C: Replace CLIP with IS because they measure the same property
questions.choice_D: Compute CLIP score only on a handful of cherry-picked examples to save time

questions.question: Compared to raw $L_2$ landmark error, what is an advantage of PCK@$\alpha$ (Percentage of Correct Keypoints at a threshold)?
questions.choice_A: It requires no ground-truth landmarks
questions.choice_B: It directly measures text-image alignment
questions.choice_C: It is identical to IoU for keypoints
questions.choice_D: It is thresholded and normalized (e.g., by object scale), making it more interpretable and robust to outliers

questions.question: What do precision and recall for generative models (in feature space) aim to disentangle compared to FID?
questions.choice_A: Precision reflects sample quality/local fidelity; recall reflects coverage/diversity of the real data manifold
questions.choice_B: Precision reflects text alignment; recall reflects image realism
questions.choice_C: Precision reflects pixel-level accuracy; recall reflects classifier accuracy
questions.choice_D: Precision and recall are identical to IS and FID respectively

questions.question: Which practice best mitigates cherry-picking in qualitative evaluation of generative models?
questions.choice_A: Selecting the most visually appealing samples for the paper
questions.choice_B: Letting annotators choose their favorite prompts
questions.choice_C: Using preregistered prompts and fixed random seeds or a hidden test set with standardized sampling
questions.choice_D: Only reporting failure cases

questions.question: Which reporting protocol most strengthens claims in generative image evaluations?
questions.choice_A: Reporting a single metric without error bars to keep the narrative simple
questions.choice_B: Providing means and confidence intervals over multiple runs, ablations, and clear descriptions of evaluation code and data
questions.choice_C: Replacing human studies with CLIP scores in all cases
questions.choice_D: Avoiding statistical tests to prevent p-hacking
